queries: web search: open source maintainers overwhelmed AI-generated pull requests 2026

GitHub issue search: "AI-generated" "pull requests" maintainers is:issue (sorted by reactions)
GitHub repo search: ai slop pull request / detect ai generated pull requests / pr spam github action / anti-slop / vouch
GitHub code search: repo:github/docs "disable pull requests" / "interaction limits"
raw fetch: AI policies of ghostty, llvm, qemu, linux, curl (3 docs), godot, scikit-learn, zulip; READMEs of vouch, fossier, pr-slop-filter
errors: Blocked by the session's network policy: bleepingcomputer.com, theregister.com, opensourceforu.com, daniel.haxx.se. News coverage of curl and Godot couldn't be read.
404: python/devguide generative-ai page and servo/book contributing page (moved or renamed). Not used.
Direct GitHub API reads of other repositories aren't permitted in this session, so issue bodies were retrieved through the GitHub search API.
Web-search result summaries were used only as leads, never as evidence, because they aren't verbatim source text.
limitations: The evidence is mostly project policy documents and maintainer statements. They show stated burden and motivation, not measured PR volumes or time costs.
Selection bias: projects that wrote policies are those most affected. Projects reporting no problem are under-represented.
No quantitative data on volumes or acceptance rates was retrieved, and no figures are claimed.
Competitor scan limited to GitHub repository search; commercial products (e.g. code-review vendors, bug-bounty platform triage) were not examined.
GitHub's newer PR-management features that news reports mention couldn't be verified beyond the docs pages retrieved.

usage.note: Performed interactively in a Claude Code session under the owner's subscription. Model calls and token counts aren't observable from inside the session, so none are reported. No API charges were incurred.
